sk-c89d0b9d.stem: To which bone does the cribriform plate belong, and what passes through it?
sk-c89d0b9d.explanation: The perforated horizontal plate of the ethmoid forms the roof of the nasal cavity; the olfactory nerve fibres from the olfactory epithelium pass through it to the olfactory bulb. Anterior skull base fractures cause anosmia and CSF rhinorrhoea.

sk-64b9533f.stem: Where does the maxillary sinus open into the nasal cavity?
sk-64b9533f.explanation: The frontal, maxillary and anterior ethmoidal sinuses open into the middle meatus (hiatus semilunaris). The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus, the posterior ethmoidal cells into the superior meatus and the sphenoidal sinus into the sphenoethmoidal recess. Because the opening of the maxillary sinus is high up, it drains poorly.
notes: It is where the sphenoidal sinus opens.
It is where the posterior ethmoidal cells open.
It is where the auditory tube opens.
It is where the nasolacrimal duct opens.

sk-114a7cc4.stem: Where does the nasolacrimal duct open into the nasal cavity?
sk-114a7cc4.explanation: The duct descending from the lacrimal sac passes through a bony canal formed by the maxilla, lacrimal bone and inferior nasal concha and opens into the meatus below the inferior concha; this is why the nose runs when we cry.

sk-ba5a5737.stem: To which bone does the thin lamina papyracea of the medial orbital wall belong?
sk-ba5a5737.explanation: The paper-thin orbital plate forming the outer surface of the ethmoidal labyrinth makes up most of the medial orbital wall. Ethmoid sinusitis can spread through this thin wall into the orbit and cause orbital cellulitis.

sk-7b06e8ab.stem: Between which bones is the lambdoid suture?
options: The occipital bone and the two parietal bones
The frontal bone and the two parietal bones
The temporal bone and the parietal bone
The sphenoid and the frontal bone
sk-7b06e8ab.explanation: The lambdoid suture runs between the occipital and parietal bones in the shape of the Greek letter λ; the point where it meets the sagittal suture is the lambda, where the posterior fontanelle closes. The other options are the coronal, sagittal and squamous sutures.
notes: This is the sagittal suture.
This is the coronal suture.
This is the squamous suture.
This is the sphenofrontal suture.

sk-66a5569f.stem: Which projection in front of the mandibular foramen gives attachment to the sphenomandibular ligament?
sk-66a5569f.explanation: The lingula is a tongue-shaped bony projection on the inner surface of the ramus that overlaps the mandibular foramen from in front. In an inferior alveolar block the needle tip is directed just above the lingula; the inferior alveolar nerve enters the canal here.

sk-e39de62d.stem: Which muscles attach to the mental spines of the mandible?
options: Mylohyoid and the anterior belly of digastric
sk-e39de62d.explanation: Genioglossus attaches to the superior mental spine and geniohyoid to the inferior mental spine, in the midline on the inner surface of the mandible. Mylohyoid attaches to the mylohyoid line and the anterior belly of digastric to the digastric fossa.

sk-4fa063c1.stem: Which structure forms the posterior wall of the sella turcica?
sk-4fa063c1.explanation: The tuberculum sellae lies in front of the sella turcica and the dorsum sellae behind it; the upper corners of the dorsum form the posterior clinoid processes. The slope descending behind the dorsum is the clivus.

options: The greater wings of the sphenoid
The body of the sphenoid and the basilar part of the occipital bone
The petrous part of the temporal bone and the occipital bone
sk-a994d076.explanation: The clivus is the sloping surface from the dorsum sellae to the foramen magnum; its upper part is the body of the sphenoid, its lower part the basilar part of the occipital bone. The pons and basilar artery lie on it; the spheno-occipital synchondrosis between them ossifies at puberty.

sk-244fa846.stem: Which nerves pass through the internal acoustic meatus?
sk-244fa846.explanation: The facial nerve (with the nervus intermedius), the vestibulocochlear nerve and the labyrinthine artery pass through the internal acoustic meatus in the petrous part of the temporal bone. An acoustic neuroma here can cause both hearing and facial nerve signs.

sk-fa671396.stem: Which bone forms the medial wall of the pterygopalatine fossa?
sk-fa671396.explanation: The pterygopalatine fossa has the maxillary tuberosity in front, the pterygoid process behind and the perpendicular plate of the palatine bone medially. The sphenopalatine foramen in the medial wall connects the fossa with the nasal cavity; the fossa contains the pterygopalatine ganglion and the last part of the maxillary artery.
notes: It forms the posterior wall.
It forms the anterior wall.
It is part of the nasal septum.
It does not border the fossa.

sk-11e451f6.stem: The foramen transversarium is characteristic of which vertebrae?
sk-11e451f6.explanation: The vertebral artery and vein pass through the foramina in the transverse processes of the cervical vertebrae; the artery usually enters at C6, and only the vein passes through the foramen of C7. This foramen is the most reliable feature distinguishing cervical vertebrae from the others.

sk-2f1cd430.stem: Which are the distinguishing features of lumbar vertebrae?
options: Large kidney-shaped body, thick rectangular spinous process and articular facets in the sagittal plane
A ring shape without a body
Bifid spinous process and foramen transversarium
sk-2f1cd430.explanation: Lumbar vertebrae have the largest bodies because they bear weight; their articular facets lie in the sagittal plane, allowing flexion–extension and limiting rotation. The other options belong to thoracic vertebrae, cervical vertebrae, the atlas and the axis.
notes: This is a feature of the axis.
This is a feature of thoracic vertebrae.
This is a feature of the atlas.
This is a feature of cervical vertebrae.

sk-66abc394.stem: At what level does the spinal cord usually end in adults?
sk-66abc394.explanation: In adults the conus medullaris ends at the level of L1–L2; in newborns at L3. The dural sac and subarachnoid space extend to S2, which is why lumbar puncture is performed below the cord, at the level of the cauda equina.
notes: This is where the dural sac ends.
This is the level in newborns.
The cord extends below this level.
The cord does not reach this level.
